title: Iminodiacetic acid stabilized 3d-4f clusters: Synthesis, structure, and magnetism
claim: Building-block assembly gives only partial structural control in the IDA system; function-specific heterometallic clusters still require real-time observation of assembly, which soft-ionization high-resolution mass spectrometry can supply.
explanation: The conclusion distinguishes geometric building-block control from true functional customization. Evolutionary mechanisms are not fully known, and trial-and-error variable spaces remain large. Soft ionization HRMS is cited as a method that has worked for related cluster systems.
scope: Synthetic control and mechanism studies of IDA 3d-4f clusters.
conditions: In-process monitoring, exemplified by soft-ionization high-resolution mass spectrometry.
caveats: The mass-spectrometry examples cited for formation dynamics are not all IDA 3d-4f clusters.
